Out of this your great an I infinite deſire, let yout rongues ſound and ſing diuine praiſes, as wel vvith voice, as muſical inſtrumentsvVherof ſix moſt vſual in the Tabernacle and Temple vvere theſe : Trumpet, Pſalter, Harpe, Timbrel, Organ and Cymbal. † Prayſe ye him on timbrel and quire: prayſe ye him on ſtringes, and organ. Ay the vvay the Pſalmiſt interpoſech agane tvvo eſpecial thinges, vvhich make perfect har- monie, vvithout vvhich no inſtrument is grarful to God: Vnitie amongſt his ſe ruants, ſign fed by the Quire of conſonant voices:h and mortification of paſſions, ſigniſi ed by Stringes, vvhich are made of de ad beaſtes bovvels. † Prayſe ye him on wel ſounding cymbals : prayſe ye him on cymbales of iubilation : † let cuerie ſpirit prayſe our Lord. Alleluia. Man created of cortuptible bodie and immortal ſoule, is finally admoniſhed to praiſe our Lord, ouer and aboue the praiſes of al other corporal creatures: vvho alſo is mote eſpecially bond therto then Angels, becauſe God hath vourſaffed to make h mſelfe Man, to redeme man that vras loſt by ſinne, and to endew him vvith nevv grace, and ſo bring him to euer- laſting glorie, vvhere vvith holie Angels, men alſo for euer & euer ſhal praiſe our Lord, vvith hart, voice, and iubilation of ſpirite, ſinging as the Pſalmiſt coneludeth, Alleluia. ANNOTATIONS. PSALME CL. The number. S. Auguſtin in the concluſion of his Enatrations, or Seimons vpon the Pſal- of Pſalmes mes, explicateth a myſterie in the number of an hundred and fiefue, ſignifyiug ſignifieth the ihe concord of the two Teſtaments. For in the old teſtament they kept the agrement ef Sabbath, which is the ſeuenth day : in the new we kepe our Lordi day, after the the old and ſabbath, that is, the eight: which ſeuen and eghmaking ſefene mul- nevv Teſta- plied by tenne, ſignifying the Law of tenne commandmentt, riſe vnto igo. ment. Againeſeuen multiplied by ſeuen make wherto one (to witte the cight) being added make fieſtie, which multiplied by three, ſigaiſying the B Trinitie, Three fifeties Make Neither ſemed it without cauſe to this great Doctor , that the firſt ſignifie Fenance. Mercie fiefue end with a Pſalme of Panance, crauing mercie & remiſſion of ſinnes: the ſecond with Mercie ind Iuſtice, which God ioyneth in the Redemption, Iuſti- fication, and Saluation of men: the laſt with Diuine Praiſes, ſigniſying, that by vrith iuſtice, condemning ſinnes in our ſelues, through Guds mercie we may be iuſined, and and Praiſes of ſo beginne in this life, which is to be perfected in the next, to praiſe our Lord, as God. Gloua Patri: added by tra- dito S Paul admoniſheth wich Pſalmes, Hymnes, and Spititual Songues. Couclu Colle ding with the vvo verſes, appointed by S. Damaſus Pope, to be added in Grra- the end of aI Pſalmes, and is obſerued ener ſince his time by tradition in the vvhole Cherch: Glorie to the Father, and to the Sonne, and to the Holie Ghoſt : As it was in the beginning, and now, and euer, into worldes of worldes I in eternitie vvithout end I Amen.
